chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about sea water — is it purifying? He said: Yes.

key_terms.طَهُور: Tahur — ritually purifying water capable of removing ritual impurity (najasa); a higher status than merely 'pure' (tahir)
key_terms.مَاءُ الْبَحْرِ: Sea water — water of the ocean or large saltwater body

ai.seo_question: Is sea water considered tahur (purifying) for wudu and ghusl in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether sea water is ritually purifying (tahur). The Imam affirms with a simple 'Yes,' establishing that sea water is pure and may be used for ritual purification (wudu and ghusl). This ruling was significant in the early Islamic community as scholars debated the rulings regarding different types of water, and the Imam's categorical affirmation settled the matter definitively.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Bak Al Hazramy who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sea water, ‘Is it clean?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isa from ‘Uthman ibn ’Isa from abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is sea water clean?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, it is clean.’”
